conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. I'm Dr. Lee, one of the hospitalists. You're here because of right flank pain. Can you tell me more about it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s been hurting for a few days now. It’s on my right side, kind of deep. It got worse yesterday.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Any fever, chills, or nausea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I don’t think so. No fever. Just the pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. You have a history of neurogenic bladder and a Foley catheter. That can sometimes cause flank pain if there’s an infection or stones.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had this before. Last time they said it might be pyelonephritis, but I had to leave for a court hearing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And you said you didn’t have pain meds after you left?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, and it was really bad. I regret leaving now. I want to stay this time and get it sorted.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad you’re here. We’ll make sure you’re comfortable and figure this out.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve drawn some blood and sent a urine sample. Your white blood cell count is normal, which is good—no sign of active infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But the urine showed something, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the urine culture grew gram-negative rods and some yeast. But given you have no fever or urinary symptoms, this may be colonization, not infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I don’t need antibiotics?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not right now. Starting antibiotics without clear infection can lead to resistance, which we want to avoid.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. Last time they gave me vancomycin for blood bacteria.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your blood cultures from the last admission grew Corynebacterium. That’s likely from your central line. We’re monitoring, but no new positive cultures this time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know I’ve been in and out a lot. I just keep getting pulled away.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We understand your situation. The goal is to help you stay healthy between visits.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also did a chest X-ray this morning. It’s clear—no pneumonia or fluid.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been coughing a little, but it’s not bad.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good to know. We’ll keep an eye on it, but nothing concerning now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve scheduled a renal ultrasound to check for kidney stones or swelling.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will that hurt?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, it’s painless. Just an ultrasound probe on your back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The ultrasound is back. Good news—no kidney stones or hydronephrosis. Your kidneys look normal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So what’s causing the pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It might be musculoskeletal or related to your chronic conditions. We’re also checking for vaginal yeast, since you mentioned discomfort there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I’ve had that before. Itches a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We gave you a single dose of Diflucan for vaginal candidiasis. That should help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. And for the flank pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re using Toradol and Percocet. Are they helping?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, much better now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also saw your potassium was high earlier—8.1—but it corrected to 3.6 after recheck. Likely a lab error, but we’re watching it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that dangerous?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: High potassium can be, but since it corrected and you feel fine, we don’t think it’s real. We’ll check again tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your repeat labs are stable. No signs of infection. We think your pain is not from the kidneys or a serious infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I can go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. We’re discharging you. We’re giving you naproxen for pain. Take it as needed, twice a day for up to a week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And if the pain comes back?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Come back if you develop fever, chills, blood in urine, or can’t urinate. Also if you can’t eat or start vomiting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about the frostbite pain in my feet?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re continuing ibuprofen, Neurontin, and Sarna lotion for that. Keep your feet warm and dry.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Social work said they found me a shelter?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, they’ve arranged a spot for you. It’s important to have a safe place to rest and recover.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I really appreciate that. I’ll try to stay out of the hospital unless I really need to.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re here to help. Just follow up if things change. Take care.
